summary.text: Three kinds of candidates emerge when CPTAC tumor-versus-normal omics, the literature corpus and external knowledge are integrated. First, established ccRCC drug targets whose evidence is genetic and clinical rather than expression-based: HIF-2α (EPAS1, belzutifan approved), the VEGF receptor KDR (multiple approved tyrosine kinase inhibitors) and MTOR. Second, HIF-driven surface or secreted proteins with large, layer-concordant increases in tumors and an existing clinical modality: CA9 (girentuximab, phase 3) and CD70 (cusatuzumab and antibody–drug conjugates). Third, metabolic tissue biomarkers that capture the clear-cell phenotype (NDUFA4L2/COXFA4L2, PLIN2, ENO2, NNMT, SLC16A3) or the loss of proximal-tubule identity (ALDOB).

CA9 is the candidate with the most complete convergence. It is increased at RNA (log2FC 6.31), protein (2.27) and phosphoprotein level, RNA and protein agree across tumors (Spearman ρ 0.80), the literature supports CA9-targeted PET imaging, and an anti-CA9 antibody has reached phase 3. Its weakness is the absence of Open Targets germline or somatic genetic evidence, which lowers it to rank 10 in the deterministic score.

The deterministic ranking places EGFR, CD74, FAS, CXCR4 and PIGR at the top. These genes show modest but concordant expression changes and receive a uniform Open Targets somatic-mutation score that is not specific to ccRCC. Several of them are expressed by infiltrating immune cells (CXCR4, CD74). They are tractable but have little or no ccRCC-specific literature in this corpus, so they are presented as hypotheses rather than priorities.

omics.text: The CPTAC discovery cohort reproduces the canonical VHL–HIF biology. VHL lies on 3p, which is lost in 79 % of tumors, and the HIF targets CA9 and NDUFA4L2 (HGNC COXFA4L2) carry the largest tumor-versus-normal changes in the dataset (RNA log2FC 6.31 and 6.75; protein 2.27 and 3.77).

Beyond hypoxia, the proteome captures the metabolic rewiring of ccRCC. Glycolysis and lactate export rise (ENO2 protein log2FC 2.25; SLC16A3/MCT4 2.28), as do lipid-droplet formation (PLIN2 2.67) and NNMT (2.71). ALDOB falls (protein log2FC −2.27; RNA −7.03), marking the loss of proximal-tubule identity.

VHL and PBRM1 illustrate why expression-based convergence misses genetic drivers. Both are lost with 3p in about 80 % of tumors, yet their protein levels barely change (VHL log2FC −0.17; PBRM1 −0.27).

literature.text: Translational literature in this corpus is strongest for CA9 (tumor-cell enrichment with low normal-kidney expression and CA9-directed PET imaging) and for NDUFA4L2, which predicts poor survival and promotes glycolysis. Most other literature-supported candidates rest on single retrospective or bioinformatic studies.

The corpus contains contradictions that a single score would hide. MT1G is reported both as downregulated in tumors and as a marker of poor prognosis, and for PFKP increased expression in tumors coexists with a report linking low expression to worse survival.

external.text: Open Targets identifies the targets already exploited clinically in ccRCC: EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved), KDR (approved VEGFR inhibitors) and MTOR (approved rapalog). They rank 9, 13 and 6 of 1,998 targets associated with ccRCC.
MET combines omics support with strong druggability. It is increased in RNA, protein and phosphoprotein, and approved inhibitors exist (cabozantinib, already used in ccRCC, and tepotinib).

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge agree most clearly on CA9: all three agents independently selected it, and it is the only candidate with expression, literature and a late-stage clinical modality at once. CD70 and NDUFA4L2 follow, with strong omics and literature support but early or no clinical drugs.

The evidence streams disagree in systematic ways. The established drug targets (EPAS1, KDR, MTOR) have genetic and clinical support but weak bulk-expression changes. The top omics genes have little ccRCC literature. Immune-related genes in the ranking (CXCR4, CD74) may reflect infiltration rather than tumor-cell expression. Prioritization therefore requires judgment across streams, not a single score.

targets.rationale: Largest concordant multi-layer increase (RNA log2FC 6.31, protein 2.27, ρ 0.80), membrane enzyme, CA9-PET literature, girentuximab phase 3. Ranked 10 by the deterministic score only because it lacks germline or somatic genetic evidence.
HIF-2α, the direct effector of VHL loss; belzutifan approved. Little bulk-expression change, so the omics stream underrates it.
VEGFR2, the backbone of ccRCC therapy, with many approved inhibitors; Open Targets rank 13.
Surface ligand up in RNA (log2FC 4.46) and protein (2.42) with the highest RNA–protein concordance among candidates (ρ 0.84); antibody and ADC programs exist.
Up in RNA, protein and phosphoprotein; approved inhibitors including cabozantinib, already used in ccRCC.
Established ccRCC pathway with an approved rapalog; Open Targets rank 6. Driven by pathway activation, not expression change.
NDUFA4L2: the largest RNA and protein increase in the cohort (log2FC 6.75 and 3.77) and literature linking it to poor survival and glycolysis. Excellent tissue biomarker; no drug yet.
MCT4 lactate exporter up in RNA (log2FC 3.44) and protein (2.28); a membrane transporter consistent with the glycolytic phenotype, a plausible metabolic target.
Lipid-droplet protein up in protein (log2FC 2.67); validated in an IHC diagnostic panel in the literature.
Glycolytic enzyme up in protein (log2FC 2.25), reported as a diagnostic and prognostic marker.
Strongest decrease (RNA log2FC −7.03; protein −2.27): a negative tissue biomarker of proximal-tubule identity loss, not a target.

Top of the deterministic ranking (modest but concordant increases, 7p gain, tractable), but no ccRCC literature in the corpus and only a non-specific somatic score: a hypothesis to test, not a priority.

limitations.text: Single discovery cohort (CPTAC, 110 tumors) without independent validation; bulk tissue comparisons mix tumor-cell and microenvironment signals.
Somatic mutation data were outside the data scope, so mutational drivers (VHL, PBRM1, SETD2, BAP1, KDM5C) are captured only through 3p loss and Open Targets.
The literature corpus has ~320 abstracts and was searched for the top omics genes, so absence of literature for a gene is not evidence of absence.
Open Targets assigns a uniform somatic-mutation score (0.456) to many cancer-census genes, which inflates the genetics stream for genes without ccRCC-specific mutation evidence.
Copy-number frequencies below 0.3 are reported in agent statements but have no evidence record in the graph.

Drug stages are reported for any indication, not specifically for ccRCC. LLM steps (relation extraction, agent analyses, this narrative) are not bit-reproducible; their outputs are saved and every statement was verified against the graph.
